strokeOrder: draw the left vertical from top to bottom, then without lifting turn and flick up to the right
lift, draw the bar from left to right
lift, begin at the top and run the long vertical down through the bar, then sweep it away to the lower left
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03052 file records げ as five stroke paths in this order and direction: け's three strokes (the left vertical with its flick, the bar and the long right stroke), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are four pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03052.svg, hiragana げ (U+3052 HIRAGANA LETTER GE), five stroke paths kvg:03052-s1 to s5 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s3 are け's strokes, the same paths as in its file for け, kanji/03051.svg; s4 and s5 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. Where the print glyph's left vertical runs on below the point the flick leaves it, the path goes down to the foot of that ink and climbs back a short way before the flick.

notes: け voiced. Opens げつようび, Monday, and げんき, well.
